title: (Old) A "Stunning" Love Letter to Viral Texts
subtitle: The Raftsman's Journal, Clearfield, PA, November 4, 1868
intro:
Like most nineteenth-century newspapers, *The Raftsman's Journal* sought to connect its readers in rural Clearfield, Pennsylvania with wider worlds of news, information, and literature. Newspaper editors subscribed to each others' newspapers, then clipped and reprinted content their readers would appreciate — sometimes changing the text in the process. Texts of all kinds circulated this way, connecting readers from New England to New Orleans to California.

This exhibit hints at the breadth — and the oddities — of nineteenth-century reprinting found by the Viral Texts Project, focusing on the "sublimely 'splendiferous'" love letter reprinted in the middle of this page. Scroll through the annotations below to explore it.
credits: Exhibit created by Ryan Cordell, Jonathan Fitzgerald, and Abby Mullen for the Viral Texts Project at Northeastern University's NULab for Texts, Maps, and Networks. Newspaper page courtesy of Chronicling America / the National Digital Newspaper Program (LCCN sn85054616).

waypoints.title: A "stunning" Love Letter.
waypoints.body:
The following is sublimely 'splendiferous,' and we recommend it as a model to letter writers:

MY DEAR MISS C.—Every time I think of you [my heart flops up and down like a churn dasher](#wl-churn-dasher). Sensations of unutterable joy creep over it like [young goats over a stable roof](#wl-young-goats), and thrill through it like [Spanish needles through a pair of tow linen trowsers](#wl-spanish-needles). As [a gosling swimeth with delight in a mud-puddle, so swim I in a sea of glory](#wl-gosling). Visions of ecstatic rapture, [thicker than the hairs in a blacking brush, and brighter than the hue of the humming bird's pinions](#wl-blacking-brush), visit me in my slumbers, and borne on their visible wings, your image stands before me, and [I reach out to grasp it, like a pointer snapping at a blue bottle fly](#wl-blue-bottle-fly). When I first beheld your angelic perfections, I was bewildered, and [my brain whirled about like a bumble bee under a glass tumbler](#wl-bumble-bee). [My eyes stood open like cellar doors in a country town](#wl-cellar-doors), and I lifted up my ears to catch the silvery accents of your voice. My tongue refused to wag, and in silent adoration [I drank in the sweet infection of love as a thirsty man swalloweth a hot whiskey punch](#wl-whiskey-punch). Since the light of your face fell upon my life, I sometimes feel as if I could [lift myself up by my bootstraps to the top of the presbyterian steeple, and pull the bell rope for singing school](#wl-presbyterian-steeple). Day and night you are in my thoughts. [When Aurora, blushing like a bride, rises from her saffron couch](#wl-aurora); and when [the jay bird pipes his tuneful lay in the apple tree](#wl-jay-bird), by the spring house; when the chanticleer's shrill clarion heralds the coming morn; when [the awakened pig ariseth from his bed and grunteth](#wl-pig-ariseth), and goeth for his morning refreshments; when [the drowsy beetle wheels his drowning flight, at sultry noontide](#wl-beetle-drowning), and when the lowing cows come home at milking time, I think of thee; and like a piece of gum elastic, [my heart seems to stretch clean across my bosom](#wl-gum-elastic). Your [hair is like the mane of a sorrel horse, powdered with gold](#wl-sorrel-horse); and [the brass pin skewered through your waterfall, fills me with unbounded awe](#wl-unbounded-awe). Your forehead is smoothar than the elbow of an old coat. Your eyes are glorious to behold. [In their liquid depths I see legions of little Cupids](#wl-little-cupids), [bathing like a cohort of ants in an old army cracker](#wl-army-cracker). When their fire hit upon my manly breast, [it penetrated my entire anatomy like a load of bird-shot would go thro a rotten apple](#wl-rotten-apple). Your nose is from a chunk of Parian marble, and your mouth puckered with sweetness. [Nectar lingers on your lips like honey on a bear's paw](#wl-bears-paw), and [myriads of unfledged kisses are there ready to fly out and light somewhere, like blue birds out of the parent's nest](#wl-blue-birds). [Your laugh rings on my ears like the wind-harp's strains, or the bleat of a stray lamb on the bleak hillside](#wl-wind-harp). [The dimples in your cheek are like bowers in beds of roses](#wl-bowers-roses), or hollows in a cake of home-made sugar.

I am dying to fly to your presence and [pour out the burning eloquence of my love, as a thrifty house wife pours out coffee](#wl-eloquence-coffee). Away from you I am as [melancholy as a sick rat](#wl-sick-rat). Sometimes I can hear [the June bugs of despondency buzzing in my ears](#wl-june-bugs), and feel [the cold lizards of despair crawling down my back](#wl-cold-lizards). [Uncouth feats, like a thousand minnows, nibble at my spirits](#wl-thousand-minnows), and my soul is [pierced through with doubts, as an old cheese with skippers](#wl-cheese-skippers).

[My love for you is stronger than the smell of Coffy's patent butter, or the kick of a young cow](#wl-coffys-butter), and [more unselfish than a kitten's first caterwaul](#wl-caterwaul). As the song bird hankers for the light of day, [the cautious mouse for the fresh bacon in the trap, as a lean pup hankers after new milk](#wl-lean-pup), so I long for thee.

You are [fairer than a speckled pullet, sweeter than a yankee doughnut fried in sorgum molasses](#wl-speckled-pullet), [brighter than the topknot plumage in the head of a muscovy duck](#wl-muscovy-duck). You are [candy kisses, raisins, pound cake and sweetened toddy altogether](#wl-candy-kisses).

If these few remarks will enable you to see the inside of my soul, and me to win your affections, I shall be as [happy as a woodpecker on a cherry tree, or a stage horse in a green pasture](#wl-woodpecker). If you cannot reciprocate my thrilling passion, I will [pine away like a poisoned bedbug](#wl-poisoned-bedbug), and [falling away from the flourishing vine of life, and untimely branch](#wl-untimely-branch); and in the coming years, when the shadows grow from the hills, and [the philisophic frog sings his cheerful evening hymns](#wl-frog-hymns), you, happy in another's love, [can come and drop a tear and catch a cold upon the last resting place of](#wl-catch-a-cold),

[JULIUS EPAMINONDAS MUGGINS.](#wl-signature)

waypoints.title: Marjorie's Almanac
waypoints.body: In the paper's "Select Poetry" column, well above the love letter, ran this seasonal verse cycling through the year — *"Don't you think that May-time's / Pleasanter than March?"* Poetry like this, easily clipped and reset in a single column, was some of the most widely and durably reprinted content in the exchange network — as portable as the love letter itself, just quieter about it.

waypoints.title: Who Ate Roger Williams?
waypoints.body: A short curiosity lifted from a chemistry textbook: when Rhode Island founder Roger Williams's grave was opened, his body was found to have dissolved entirely — replaced by the roots of a nearby apple tree, grown down through where his coffin had been. Macabre-but-instructive filler like this circulated in the very same exchange network that carried the love letter.

waypoints.title: Hoofland's German Bitters
waypoints.body: Patent-medicine advertising like this — promising to cure "all diseases of the Liver, Stomach, or digestive organs" — was a fixture of nineteenth-century newspaper pages, often running unchanged for months. A reminder that not everything reprinted on a page like this one was "viral" in the same playful sense as the love letter; some content simply paid for its own repetition.
